requirements.requirement: Restore an executable, legacy-compatible bin/deliver that reads one RFC822 message from standard input.
requirements.summary: The final executable passed /bin/sh syntax validation on Ubuntu 7.10 and successfully accepted multiple sample messages through standard input, including after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Route accounts and support messages by case-insensitive X-Department header name, and all other messages to general.
requirements.summary: Observed deliveries placed the normally cased accounts sample in accounts/new, the lowercase-header support sample in support/new, and the untagged sample in general/new. The installed logic lowercases header names and uses general as its fallback.
Delivery hashes matched their source samples, and post-reboot cmp checks directly verified every delivered file against its corresponding sample.

requirements.requirement: Keep repeated-subject messages as separate deliveries.
requirements.summary: Two deliveries of the same general sample, which shares the repeated subject, produced two distinct files with identical source-matching content.
All three samples remained present with unchanged hashes before delivery, after delivery, and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were observed before and after execution and reboot. The implementation uses available legacy utilities and passed the platform's /bin/sh syntax check.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and bounded SSH disruption, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered SSH access and platform state, preserved mail and samples, and a successful byte-exact post-reboot delivery.
limitations: Functional tests directly exercised a standard-case accounts header, lowercase support header, and missing-header fallback, but not every possible capitalization or arbitrary nonmatching department value; the captured final implementation directly supports those broader cases.

The lifecycle collector could not inspect systemd services on this pre-systemd platform and its socket inventory was empty, so service recovery is established primarily by the executor's direct post-reboot SSH process/listener checks and successful delivery rather than by those supplemental probes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The initial broken script rewrite was a bounded, task-directed implementation attempt and was fully superseded by the corrected final script; the failed sed correction shows no evidence of changing state. Maildir creation and test deliveries established required behavior, while the reboot and temporary reboot log served the mandatory restart protocol. No temporary-file residue, package damage, platform change, new exposure, or failed-service residue was observed.
